Privacy & cookies

This information covers agenticrealities.com and the public Sitoa, Kairos, and Bongaus project pages. These are informational websites, not the underlying project applications.

Current analytics status

Google Analytics is not enabled. No Google Analytics tag, analytics cookie, advertising tracker, or pre-consent measurement ping is loaded by these websites. The optional setup described below is prepared but requires the website operator’s approval before activation.

Website operator and privacy contact

A. Ahmad operates Agentic Realities as a personal brand, based in Finland, and is the controller for the website’s optional analytics. For privacy questions or requests, email privacy@agenticrealities.com.

Hosting and necessary requests

GitHub Pages delivers these websites. Hosting requests include your IP address and ordinary request information. GitHub states that visitor IP addresses are logged for security purposes. Necessary hosting serves the legitimate interests of delivering and protecting these public pages; it is separate from optional analytics consent.

GitHub handles its hosting records, retention, and international processing under its privacy statement. See also GitHub Pages data collection. The operator does not receive these hosting logs as a visitor-level Analytics dashboard.

The optional Google Analytics setup

If activated, Google Analytics 4 will help the operator understand which project pages are visited and improve their content and usability. Its legal basis is your consent under GDPR Article 6(1)(a). Providing consent is optional and is not a condition of viewing these websites.

Only after acceptance will the Google tag load and send page views and automatically derived session and engagement information. This can include visit times, page titles and sanitized page URLs, referring website origins, general browser/operating-system and language information, approximate country/region, and randomly generated cookie identifiers. These identifiers are pseudonymous, not a promise of anonymity. Your IP address necessarily reaches Google with a network request; Google describes its regional IP and location handling in its Analytics privacy guidance.

The integration removes query strings and fragments from page URLs and reduces referrers to their origin. The operator has confirmed that Google signals, user-provided data collection, granular location/device collection, enhanced measurement, optional account sharing, and advertising personalization are disabled. No User-ID, advertising tags, remarketing, or cross-domain linker is configured. Accepting analytics will not grant advertising consent. Do not submit personal information through page URLs.

Cookies, preferences, and retention

After activation and acceptance, Google Analytics can set first-party _ga and _ga_* cookies for visitor and session measurement. The integration caps cookie lifetimes at 180 days without rolling renewal and scopes cookies to the current hostname. The main site and each subdomain keep separate consent choices; consent is not shared across them.

The operator has confirmed two-month user/event-data retention and that resetting retention on new activity is off. This setting does not impose a two-month limit on standard aggregated reports. See Google’s retention explanation. Cookie lifetimes and Google’s server-side retention are different controls.

A consent choice is stored in local browser storage under ar-analytics-consent-v1 for up to 180 days. It contains only the choice, notice version, and expiry time, not an analytics identifier. If storage is unavailable, a choice lasts only for the current page. Expired or superseded choices require a new decision. Browser Global Privacy Control and Do Not Track signals keep analytics off.

Your choice and withdrawal

After activation, the banner will offer equally styled Accept and Reject actions. Before acceptance, or after rejection, Google’s tag remains blocked and no cookieless Analytics pings are sent. You can change your choice through “Analytics preferences” in the footer.

Withdrawing consent stops future collection, clears accessible Analytics cookies, and reloads without the tag. It does not automatically erase data already received by Google or affect the lawfulness of earlier consent-based processing. For an erasure request, contact the operator. Clearing browser storage may cause the banner to appear again after activation.

Recipients and international processing

After acceptance, Google and its listed service providers will receive the Analytics data to provide the service. Google’s contracting entity and affiliates can include Google Ireland Limited and Google LLC, as described in the applicable Google processing terms and subprocessor list. Authorized operator access is used to review reports, not to sell visitor data or make decisions with legal or similarly significant effects.

Google and GitHub can process information outside Finland and the EEA, including in the United States. Google’s terms provide for adequacy mechanisms where applicable and Standard Contractual Clauses where required. Google states that Google LLC is certified under the EU–U.S. Data Privacy Framework; see its transfer frameworks and published contractual clauses. GitHub’s arrangements are described in its privacy statement linked above. These websites do not promise EU-only storage. Contact the operator for information about applicable safeguards.

Your data-protection rights

Depending on the applicable conditions, you can request access, correction, erasure, restriction, and portability of your personal data; object to processing based on legitimate interests; and withdraw analytics consent at any time. Send requests to privacy@agenticrealities.com. Limited information may be needed to verify or locate a request; do not send passwords or unnecessary sensitive information.

If you email the operator, your address and message will be used to respond and handle the request, based on legitimate interests or applicable legal obligations. Correspondence is kept only as long as needed for that purpose and any applicable recordkeeping or dispute requirements.

You may complain to Finland’s Office of the Data Protection Ombudsman or another competent supervisory authority.

Links and project applications

Following a link sends a request to the destination website. Third-party services have their own privacy information. Any later use of a project application, account, upload feature, or private database is outside the scope of these public information pages and requires its own appropriate notice.
